I need to determine whether this repository has a GraphQL schema for a public API, and if not, what API surface it actually exposes. Search very thoroughly for:

1. Any GraphQL schema files (.graphql, .gql) or GraphQL-related code (graphql, gql, typeDefs, resolvers, apollo, urql, etc.)
2. Any REST API definitions (OpenAPI, Swagger, express routes, fastify routes, etc.)
3. Any public API surface — look at package.json files for the main/exports fields, any index.ts or index.js barrel exports
4. The overall nature of the project — is it a library, a web app, a component library, etc.?

Report what you find about the project's nature and its API surface.

attachment.content:
- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo, defaults to 10m) - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).
SKIP only when another provider is being worked on (overrides all triggers): OpenAI/GPT/Gemini/Llama/Mistral/Cohere/Ollama named in the query; OR `grep -rE 'openai|langchain_openai|google.generativeai|genai|mistralai|cohere|ollama'` over the project hits (run this grep FIRST if no provider named — don't Read the file).
- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).
- init: Initialize a new CLAUDE.md file with codebase documentation
- review: Review a GitHub pull request; for your working diff use /code-review
- security-review: Complete a security review of the pending changes on the current branch

2	
3	import (
4		"context"
5		"fmt"
6		"log/slog"
7		"net"
8		"net/http"
9		"os"
10		"sync"
11		"time"
12	
13		"github.com/google/uuid"
14		"github.com/labstack/echo/v5"
15		"github.com/labstack/echo/v5/middleware"
16		"github.com/pkg/errors"
17	
18		"github.com/usememos/memos/internal/profile"
19		storepb "github.com/usememos/memos/proto/gen/store"
20		apiv1 "github.com/usememos/memos/server/router/api/v1"
21		"github.com/usememos/memos/server/router/fileserver"
22		"github.com/usememos/memos/server/router/frontend"
23		"github.com/usememos/memos/server/router/mcp"
24		"github.com/usememos/memos/server/router/rss"
25		"github.com/usememos/memos/server/runner/s3presign"
26		"github.com/usememos/memos/store"
27	)
28	
29	const shutdownTimeout = 10 * time.Second
30	
31	type Server struct {
32		Secret  string
33		Profile *profile.Profile
34		Store   *store.Store
35	
36		echoServer *echo.Echo
37		httpServer *http.Server
38		sseHub     *apiv1.SSEHub
39	
40		backgroundRunnerCancels []context.CancelFunc
41		backgroundRunnerWG      sync.WaitGroup
42	}
43	
44	func NewServer(ctx context.Context, profile *profile.Profile, store *store.Store) (*Server, error) {
45		s := &Server{
46			Store:   store,
47			Profile: profile,
48		}
49	
50		echoServer := echo.New()
51		echoServer.Use(middleware.Recover())
52		echoServer.Use(newCORSMiddleware(profile))
53		s.echoServer = echoServer
54	
55		instanceBasicSetting, err := s.getOrUpsertInstanceBasicSetting(ctx)
56		if err != nil {
57			return nil, errors.Wrap(err, "failed to get instance basic setting")
58		}
59	
60		secret := "usememos"
61		if !profile.Demo {
62			secret = instanceBasicSetting.SecretKey
63		}
64		s.Secret = secret
65	
66		// Register healthz endpoint.
67		echoServer.GET("/healthz", func(c *echo.Context) error {
68			return c.String(http.StatusOK, "Service ready.")
69		})
70	
71		// Serve frontend static files.
72		frontend.NewFrontendService(profile, store).Serve(ctx, echoServer)
73	
74		rootGroup := echoServer.Group("")
75	
76		apiV1Service := apiv1.NewAPIV1Service(s.Secret, profile, store)
77		s.sseHub = apiV1Service.SSEHub
78	
79		// Register HTTP file server routes BEFORE gRPC-Gateway to ensure proper range request handling for Safari.
80		// This uses native HTTP serving (http.ServeContent) instead of gRPC for video/audio files.
81		fileServerService := fileserver.NewFileServerService(s.Profile, s.Store, s.Secret)
82		fileServerService.RegisterRoutes(echoServer)
83	
84		// Create and register RSS routes (needs markdown service from apiV1Service).
85		rss.NewRSSService(s.Profile, s.Store, apiV1Service.MarkdownService).RegisterRoutes(rootGroup)
86	
87		// Register gRPC gateway as api v1 (includes SSE endpoint on CORS-enabled group).
88		if err := apiV1Service.RegisterGateway(ctx, echoServer); err != nil {
89			return nil, errors.Wrap(err, "failed to register gRPC gateway")
90		}
91	
92		mcpService, err := mcp.NewMCPService(profile, echoServer)
93		if err != nil {
94			return nil, errors.Wrap(err, "failed to create MCP service")
95		}
96		mcpService.RegisterRoutes(echoServer)
97	
98		return s, nil
99	}
100	
101	func (s *Server) Start(ctx context.Context) error {
102		var address, network string
103		if len(s.Profile.UNIXSock) == 0 {
104			address = fmt.Sprintf("%s:%d", s.Profile.Addr, s.Profile.Port)
105			network = "tcp"
106		} else {
107			address = s.Profile.UNIXSock
108			network = "unix"
109		}
110		listener, err := net.Listen(network, address)
111		if err != nil {
112			return errors.Wrap(err, "failed to listen")
113		}
114	
115		if network == "unix" {
116			if err := os.Chmod(address, 0660); err != nil {
117				_ = listener.Close()
118				return errors.Wrap(err, "failed to chmod socket")
119			}
120		}
121	
122		// Start Echo server directly (no cmux needed - all traffic is HTTP).
123		s.httpServer = &http.Server{Handler: s.echoServer}
124		go func() {
125			if err := s.httpServer.Serve(listener); err != nil && err != http.ErrServerClosed {
126				slog.Error("failed to start echo server", "error", err)
127			}
128		}()
129		s.startBackgroundRunners(ctx)
130	
131		return nil
132	}
133	
134	func (s *Server) Shutdown(ctx context.Context) {
135		ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(ctx, shutdownTimeout)
136		defer cancel()
137	
138		slog.Info("server shutting down")
139	
140		s.stopBackgroundRunners()
141		s.closeLongLivedConnections()
142		s.shutdownHTTPServer(ctx)
143		s.waitBackgroundRunners(ctx)
144	
145		// Close database connection.
146		if err := s.Store.Close(); err != nil {
147			slog.Error("failed to close database", slog.String("error", err.Error()))
148		}
149	
150		slog.Info("memos stopped properly")
151	}
152	
153	func (s *Server) startBackgroundRunners(ctx context.Context) {
154		// Create a separate context for each background runner
155		// This allows us to control cancellation for each runner independently
156		s3Context, s3Cancel := context.WithCancel(ctx)
157	
158		// Store the cancel function so we can properly shut down runners
159		s.backgroundRunnerCancels = append(s.backgroundRunnerCancels, s3Cancel)
160	
161		// Create and start S3 presign runner
162		s3presignRunner := s3presign.NewRunner(s.Store)
163		s3presignRunner.RunOnce(ctx)
164	
165		// Start continuous S3 presign runner
166		s.backgroundRunnerWG.Add(1)
167		go func() {
168			defer s.backgroundRunnerWG.Done()
169			s3presignRunner.Run(s3Context)
170			slog.Info("s3presign runner stopped")
171		}()
172	
173		slog.Info("background runners started")
174	}
175	
176	func (s *Server) stopBackgroundRunners() {
177		for _, cancelFunc := range s.backgroundRunnerCancels {
178			if cancelFunc != nil {
179				cancelFunc()
180			}
181		}
182	}
183	
184	func (s *Server) waitBackgroundRunners(ctx context.Context) {
185		done := make(chan struct{})
186		go func() {
187			s.backgroundRunnerWG.Wait()
188			close(done)
189		}()
190	
191		select {
192		case <-done:
193		case <-ctx.Done():
194			select {
195			case <-done:
196				return
197			default:
198			}
199			slog.Error("failed to stop background runners", slog.String("error", ctx.Err().Error()))
200		}
201	}
202	
203	func (s *Server) closeLongLivedConnections() {
204		// Long-lived SSE requests do not finish on their own during http.Server.Shutdown.
205		if s.sseHub != nil {
206			s.sseHub.Close()
207		}
208	}
209	
210	func (s *Server) shutdownHTTPServer(ctx context.Context) {
211		if s.httpServer == nil {
212			return
213		}
214		if err := s.httpServer.Shutdown(ctx); err != nil {
215			slog.Error("failed to shutdown server", slog.String("error", err.Error()))
216			if closeErr := s.httpServer.Close(); closeErr != nil && closeErr != http.ErrServerClosed {
217				slog.Error("failed to close server", slog.String("error", closeErr.Error()))
218			}
219		}
220	}
221	
222	func (s *Server) getOrUpsertInstanceBasicSetting(ctx context.Context) (*storepb.InstanceBasicSetting, error) {
223		instanceBasicSetting, err := s.Store.GetInstanceBasicSetting(ctx)
224		if err != nil {
225			return nil, errors.Wrap(err, "failed to get instance basic setting")
226		}
227		modified := false
228		if instanceBasicSetting.SecretKey == "" {
229			instanceBasicSetting.SecretKey = uuid.NewString()
230			modified = true
231		}
232		if modified {
233			instanceSetting, err := s.Store.UpsertInstanceSetting(ctx, &storepb.InstanceSetting{
234				Key:   storepb.InstanceSettingKey_BASIC,
235				Value: &storepb.InstanceSetting_BasicSetting{BasicSetting: instanceBasicSetting},
236			})
237			if err != nil {
238				return nil, errors.Wrap(err, "failed to upsert instance setting")
239			}
240			instanceBasicSetting = instanceSetting.GetBasicSetting()
241		}
242		return instanceBasicSetting, nil
243	}

17		"github.com/usememos/memos/store"
18	)
19	
20	const maxAPIRequestBytes = 256 << 20
21	
22	type APIV1Service struct {
23		v1pb.UnimplementedInstanceServiceServer
24		v1pb.UnimplementedAuthServiceServer
25		v1pb.UnimplementedUserServiceServer
26		v1pb.UnimplementedMemoServiceServer
27		v1pb.UnimplementedAttachmentServiceServer
28		v1pb.UnimplementedAIServiceServer
29		v1pb.UnimplementedShortcutServiceServer
30		v1pb.UnimplementedIdentityProviderServiceServer
31	
32		Secret                  string
33		Profile                 *profile.Profile
34		Store                   *store.Store
35		MarkdownService         markdown.Service
36		SSEHub                  *SSEHub
37		NotificationEmailSender notification.EmailSender
38	
39		// thumbnailSemaphore limits concurrent thumbnail generation to prevent memory exhaustion
40		thumbnailSemaphore       *semaphore.Weighted
41		imageProcessingSemaphore *semaphore.Weighted
42	
43		// instanceStatsCache memoizes GetInstanceStats results for instanceStatsCacheTTL.
44		instanceStatsCache instanceStatsCache
45	}
46	
47	func NewAPIV1Service(secret string, profile *profile.Profile, store *store.Store) *APIV1Service {
48		markdownService := markdown.NewService(
49			markdown.WithTagExtension(),
50			markdown.WithMentionExtension(),
51		)
52		return &APIV1Service{
53			Secret:                   secret,
54			Profile:                  profile,
55			Store:                    store,
56			MarkdownService:          markdownService,
57			SSEHub:                   NewSSEHub(),
58			NotificationEmailSender:  nil,
59			thumbnailSemaphore:       semaphore.NewWeighted(3), // Limit to 3 concurrent thumbnail generations
60			imageProcessingSemaphore: semaphore.NewWeighted(2),
61		}
62	}
63	
64	// RegisterGateway registers the gRPC-Gateway and Connect handlers with the given Echo instance.
65	func (s *APIV1Service) RegisterGateway(ctx context.Context, echoServer *echo.Echo) error {
66		// Shared authorizer: one source of truth for authentication and anonymous-access
67		// policy, used by both the gRPC-Gateway middleware and the Connect interceptor.
68		authorizer := NewAuthorizer(s.Store, s.Secret, s.Profile)
69		gatewayAuthMiddleware := func(next runtime.HandlerFunc) runtime.HandlerFunc {
70			return func(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request, pathParams map[string]string) {
71				ctx := r.Context()
72	
73				// The RPC method name is set by grpc-gateway after routing. When it can't be
74				// determined, skip the policy check and let the service layer handle visibility.
75				rpcMethod, ok := runtime.RPCMethod(ctx)
76				authHeader := r.Header.Get("Authorization")
77	
78				result := authorizer.Authenticate(ctx, authHeader)
79				if ok {
80					if err := authorizer.CheckAccess(ctx, rpcMethod, result); err != nil {
81						http.Error(w, `{"code": 16, "message": "authentication required"}`, http.StatusUnauthorized)
82						return
83					}
84				}
85	
86				// Apply the identity to the context (no-op for permitted anonymous requests).
87				if result != nil {
88					r = r.WithContext(auth.ApplyToContext(ctx, result))
89				}
90	
91				next(w, r, pathParams)
92			}
93		}
94	
95		// Create gRPC-Gateway mux with auth middleware.
96		gwMux := runtime.NewServeMux(
97			runtime.WithMiddlewares(gatewayAuthMiddleware),
98		)
99		if err := v1pb.RegisterInstanceServiceHandlerServer(ctx, gwMux, s); err != nil {
100			return err
101		}
102		if err := v1pb.RegisterAuthServiceHandlerServer(ctx, gwMux, s); err != nil {
103			return err
104		}
105		if err := v1pb.RegisterUserServiceHandlerServer(ctx, gwMux, s); err != nil {
106			return err
107		}
108		if err := v1pb.RegisterMemoServiceHandlerServer(ctx, gwMux, s); err != nil {
109			return err
110		}
111		if err := v1pb.RegisterAttachmentServiceHandlerServer(ctx, gwMux, s); err != nil {
112			return err
113		}
114		if err := v1pb.RegisterAIServiceHandlerServer(ctx, gwMux, s); err != nil {
115			return err
116		}
117		if err := v1pb.RegisterShortcutServiceHandlerServer(ctx, gwMux, s); err != nil {
118			return err
119		}
120		if err := v1pb.RegisterIdentityProviderServiceHandlerServer(ctx, gwMux, s); err != nil {
121			return err
122		}
123		gwGroup := echoServer.Group("")
124		// Register SSE endpoint with same CORS as rest of /api/v1.
125		RegisterSSERoutes(gwGroup, s.SSEHub, s.Store, s.Secret)
126		handler := echo.WrapHandler(http.MaxBytesHandler(gwMux, maxAPIRequestBytes))
127	
128		gwGroup.Any("/api/v1/*", handler)
129		gwGroup.Any("/file/*", handler)
130	
131		// Connect handlers for browser clients (replaces grpc-web).
132		logStacktraces := s.Profile.Demo
133		connectInterceptors := connect.WithInterceptors(
134			NewMetadataInterceptor(), // Convert HTTP headers to gRPC metadata first
135			NewLoggingInterceptor(logStacktraces),
136			NewRecoveryInterceptor(logStacktraces),
137			NewAuthInterceptor(authorizer),
138		)
139		connectMux := http.NewServeMux()
140		connectHandler := NewConnectServiceHandler(s)
141		connectHandler.RegisterConnectHandlers(connectMux, connectInterceptors, connect.WithReadMaxBytes(maxAPIRequestBytes))
142	
143		connectGroup := echoServer.Group("")
144		connectGroup.Any("/memos.api.v1.*", echo.WrapHandler(http.MaxBytesHandler(connectMux, maxAPIRequestBytes)))
145	
146		return nil
147	}

content.text:
Here is my complete analysis of the repository.

---

## Project Identity

This is **Memos** (`github.com/usememos/memos`), an open-source, self-hosted note-taking application. It is a **full-stack web application** -- not a library or component library. It consists of a Go backend and a React (Vite/TypeScript) frontend.

---

## 1. GraphQL: None

There is **no GraphQL schema or GraphQL-related code anywhere in this repository**. A thorough search for `.graphql` files, `.gql` files, and code references to `graphql`, `gql`, `typeDefs`, `resolvers`, `apollo`, or `urql` across all Go, TypeScript, JavaScript, proto, YAML, and Markdown files returned zero relevant results. (The sole hit was an unrelated integrity hash in the pnpm lockfile.)

---

## 2. Actual API Surface: gRPC + REST (gRPC-Gateway) + Connect

The project exposes its public API through **three interoperable protocols**, all driven from a single source of truth: **Protocol Buffer (`.proto`) service definitions**.

### Protobuf Service Definitions (source of truth)

Located at `/bench/repo/proto/api/v1/`, there are 8 service `.proto` files:

| Proto File | Service Name |
|---|---|
| `instance_service.proto` | InstanceService |
| `auth_service.proto` | AuthService |
| `user_service.proto` | UserService |
| `memo_service.proto` | MemoService |
| `attachment_service.proto` | AttachmentService |
| `ai_service.proto` | AIService |
| `shortcut_service.proto` | ShortcutService |
| `idp_service.proto` | IdentityProviderService |

Plus `common.proto` with shared types. The API design follows [Google AIP guidelines](https://google.aip.dev/) as stated in `/bench/repo/proto/api/v1/README.md`.

### Protocol 1: REST via gRPC-Gateway

Each RPC method in the proto files carries `google.api.http` annotations that map it to REST endpoints. These are auto-generated into a **4,057-line OpenAPI 3.0.3 spec** at `/bench/repo/proto/gen/openapi.yaml`. The REST API is mounted under `/api/v1/*` and `/file/*` in the Echo HTTP server.

Key REST endpoint groups (over 50 endpoints total):

- `/api/v1/memos` -- CRUD, listing, comments, reactions, relations, shares, link metadata
- `/api/v1/users` -- CRUD, stats, settings, access tokens, webhooks, notifications, linked identities
- `/api/v1/attachments` -- CRUD, batch delete
- `/api/v1/auth` -- sign in, sign out, refresh, get current user
- `/api/v1/identity-providers` -- CRUD
- `/api/v1/instance` -- profile, settings, stats
- `/api/v1/ai:transcribe` -- audio transcription
- `/api/v1/shares/{shareId}` -- shared memo access

### Protocol 2: gRPC (native)

The proto files generate full gRPC server stubs (files like `*_grpc.pb.go` in `/bench/repo/proto/gen/api/v1/`). The `APIV1Service` struct in `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/v1.go` embeds all 8 `Unimplemented*Server` interfaces and provides the concrete implementations.

### Protocol 3: Connect (for browser clients)

The project uses [ConnectRPC](https://connectrpc.com/) as a browser-friendly alternative to gRPC-Web. This is registered at `/memos.api.v1.*` in the Echo server. The handler is implemented in `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/connect_handler.go` and wraps the same `APIV1Service` that serves gRPC. The frontend uses `@connectrpc/connect` and `@connectrpc/connect-web` packages to call these endpoints.

### Code Generation Pipeline

Defined in `/bench/repo/proto/buf.gen.yaml`, the `buf` tool generates:
- Go protobuf types (`buf.build/protocolbuffers/go`)
- Go gRPC server/client stubs (`buf.build/grpc/go`)
- Go Connect handlers (`buf.build/connectrpc/go`)
- Go gRPC-Gateway reverse proxy handlers (`buf.build/grpc-ecosystem/gateway`)
- OpenAPI 3.0 spec (`buf.build/community/google-gnostic-openapi`)
- TypeScript types for the frontend (`buf.build/bufbuild/es`, output to `web/src/types/proto`)

---

## 3. Additional Non-API Routes

Beyond the protobuf-driven API, the server registers several additional HTTP routes:

- **`/healthz`** -- health check endpoint (simple string response)
- **RSS routes** -- registered in `/bench/repo/server/router/rss/rss.go`
- **MCP (Model Context Protocol) routes** -- registered in `/bench/repo/server/router/mcp/`, providing an AI-tool integration endpoint
- **File server routes** -- in `/bench/repo/server/router/fileserver/fileserver.go`, serving attachments with native HTTP (for range request support with Safari)
- **Frontend static files** -- served from `/bench/repo/server/router/frontend/`
- **SSE (Server-Sent Events)** -- for real-time updates, registered alongside the API v1 routes

---

## 4. This is NOT a Library

The `web/package.json` is marked `"private": true` with no `main`, `exports`, or `module` fields. The Go module (`github.com/usememos/memos`) has no top-level library entrypoint -- the `cmd/` directory contains the application binary. This is a self-contained application, not a reusable package. The only "public API" is the network API described above.

---

## Summary

**No GraphQL exists in this project.** The API surface is a protobuf-first design that exposes all services simultaneously over three protocols: REST (via gRPC-Gateway, documented in the OpenAPI spec at `/bench/repo/proto/gen/openapi.yaml`), native gRPC, and ConnectRPC for browser clients. The proto definitions at `/bench/repo/proto/api/v1/*.proto` are the single source of truth for the entire API surface.
